title: The January cover
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The first cover of the year: the bay from the launch in January, gray on gray, no shack, no dock, no one. The owner says there's nothing on it. Wood says look longer. She does.

panels.composition: The cover: the bay in January, gray water, gray sky, the far shore a line. Nothing else.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing a gray bay under a gray sky with a far shore as a single line, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner holding it. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a small booklet at arm's length while a young man and a dog wait, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner looking longer. The cover. A gull, tiny, that wasn't there — it was. Two strokes, mid-bay.

image.prompt: close on a booklet cover of a gray bay with a tiny two-stroke bird in the middle distance, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner setting it in the rack without a word. That's the review. The dryers.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner placing a small booklet in a wire rack without comment, dryers turning behind her, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Look longer.' The Januaries are the deepest landscapes; the strip starts that here.
